Estimate bias and interaction screening terms

Source: R/api-tables.R
estimate_bias.Rd

Estimate bias and interaction screening terms

Usage

estimate_bias(
  fit,
  diagnostics,
  facet_a = NULL,
  facet_b = NULL,
  interaction_facets = NULL,
  max_abs = 10,
  omit_extreme = TRUE,
  max_iter = 4,
  tol = 0.001,
  xtreme = 0
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Output from diagnose_mfrm(). Must match this fitted analysis; see mfrmr_compatibility_layer for migration of saved diagnostics.

facet_a

First facet name. Provide together with facet_b for the classic pairwise 2-way interaction. Ignored when interaction_facets is supplied. The canonical "Person" role is accepted explicitly.

facet_b

Second facet name. See facet_a.

interaction_facets

Character vector of two or more facets to model as one interaction effect. When supplied, this takes precedence over facet_a/facet_b. Use this form (rather than facet_a/facet_b) whenever you want 3+ way interactions, since facet_a/facet_b is restricted to the pairwise case. The canonical "Person" role may be supplied explicitly; see the Person-screening boundary below.

max_abs

Bound for absolute bias size.

omit_extreme

Omit extreme-only elements. In ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML, directly fixed finite anchors are retained even with all-low/all-high responses. Their cell bias may still have no finite unconstrained optimum.

max_iter

Maximum number of repeated cell-estimation passes recorded in iteration; the baseline calibration stays fixed throughout.

tol

Between-pass change tolerance for the iteration log. This does not control the tolerance of the bounded scalar likelihood optimizer.

xtreme

Default 0 retains bounded extreme-cell estimates with SEs withheld. A positive correction (usually .5 for FACETS bias reporting) requests finite total-score extrapolation for ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML without group-mean anchors; it must be smaller than the score range.

Value

An object of class mfrm_bias with:

  • table: interaction rows with effect size, SE, screening t/p metadata, reporting-use flags, fit columns, and GPCM profile-likelihood columns when available

  • summary: compact summary statistics

  • chi_sq: fixed-effect chi-square style screening summary

  • facet_a, facet_b: first two analyzed facet names (legacy compatibility)

  • interaction_facets, interaction_order, interaction_mode: full interaction metadata

  • person_interaction, person_source_column, person_interaction_note: Person-screening provenance and interpretation metadata

  • iteration: iteration history/metadata

  • orientation_review: facet-orientation sign-consistency review table

  • mixed_sign: logical flag indicating whether bias-size signs flip across facets in a way that complicates direction interpretation

  • direction_note: one-line interpretive note describing the dominant bias direction (empty when not applicable)

  • recommended_action: one-line recommended-action label routing the user to the appropriate follow-up helper

  • inference_tier: summary label indicating that the bias rows are intended for screening and follow-up review

  • optimization_failures: per-cell record of any inner-loop optimizer failures encountered while estimating the bias parameters; empty when every cell converged cleanly

Details

This helper supports RSM, PCM, and one-slope-family GPCM fits. Two-slope-family GPCM fits are not currently supported. It estimates an additional cell shift relative to the fitted baseline, holding that baseline fixed. For joint estimation of main effects and a two-facet interaction in RSM / PCM, use the facet_interactions argument of fit_mfrm(). For the supported fixed-population RSM/PCM MML route, mfrm_facet_intervals() with interaction = "FacetA:FacetB" returns joint-information cell intervals. They estimate a different target and do not replace or relabel this fixed-baseline screening result.

Bias (interaction) in an additive MFRM refers to a systematic departure from the main-effects model: a specific rater-criterion (or higher-order) combination produces scores that are consistently higher or lower than predicted by the main effects alone. For example, Rater A might be unexpectedly harsh on Criterion 2 despite being lenient overall.

Mathematically, the bias term \(b_{jc}\) for rater \(j\) on criterion \(c\) modifies the linear predictor:

$$\eta_{njc} = \theta_n - \delta_j - \beta_c + b_{jc}$$

Here the example uses negatively oriented rater and criterion facets. The returned Bias Size is always an additive shift in the score predictor: positive values increase expected scores; negative values decrease them. If the fitted model already contains facet_interactions, those fitted interactions remain part of the fixed baseline. The new shift is a residual departure from that model, not a re-estimate of its interaction. Each cell's shift is estimated by maximizing its conditional likelihood within [-max_abs, max_abs], holding fitted person measures, facet values, steps and slopes fixed. For RSM / PCM, an interior solution satisfies the weighted score equation:

$$\sum_n w_{njc} \{X_{njc} - E_{njc}(b_{jc})\} = 0.$$

With unit weights, \(w_{njc}=1\). The conditional information gives \(\mathrm{SE}(\hat b) = [\sum_n w_{njc} \mathrm{Var}_{njc}(\hat b)]^{-1/2}\). For GPCM, the score and information include the observation's slope and squared slope, respectively, and conditional profile-likelihood columns are also returned. Bias Size is in the model's native ability units: in RSM / PCM it equals the change in adjacent-category log odds, whereas in GPCM that change is \(a b\) for an observation with slope \(a\). The same bias value can therefore imply different probability changes across observations. All these quantities are plug-in screening evidence: JML person measures or MML EAP scores and the calibration parameters are treated as known. Their estimation uncertainty, including uncertainty in supplied anchors, is not propagated. A fixed rater severity can therefore have a nonzero cell bias and positive bias SE: the fixed severity and the cell's additional shift are different quantities. BiasStatus identifies an interior solution or an optimum at either search bound. A bounded point remains available, but its S.E., t, Prob. and GPCM profile-inference columns are withheld at a boundary. Inspect ScreenStatus and ScreenReason: a bound can mean an insufficient search range or an all-low/all-high cell with no finite unconstrained optimum. Increasing the range does not resolve the latter.

With xtreme > 0, an all-low/all-high cell's weighted total is moved inward by xtreme times its smallest positive weight. A root strictly inside [-max_abs, max_abs] yields BiasStatus = "extreme_adjusted", finite Bias Size and conditional information SE; PrimaryBias retains the infinite cell MLE and ExtremeAdjustment records the total correction. Otherwise the boundary remains unavailable for screening. Observations involving any unanchored extreme main-effect element are excluded in this route even when omit_extreme = FALSE; finite fixed anchors remain usable. This prevents main-effect display replacements from becoming calibration. The default xtreme = 0 also retains directly fixed finite anchors in ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML; extreme cells then keep bounded points with screening SEs and tail areas withheld. Group-mean constraints are not direct anchors. The native FACETS Xtreme = main,bias has two separate corrections: this function's xtreme corresponds to the second value (normally .5), not the first (normally .3). Executed FACETS 4.5.0 Person-by-Rater examples retain fixed extreme Persons and agree with the conditional cell calculation on the same main calibration. This does not establish main-calibration parity. If a low cell's baseline expectation is already below the inward correction, its adjusted bias can be positive despite a negative observed-minus-expected score difference (and conversely at the upper endpoint). Inspect PrimaryBias, ExtremeAdjustment and Obs-Exp Average together; the adjusted sign describes the amended total, not a reversal of the observed departure. Extrapolated tail areas, summaries and pairwise contrasts are reporting conventions, not regular-MLE inference, coverage guarantees or fairness tests.

ConditionalInformation uses every cell row, including small positive conditional variances; the residual-screening cutoff does not remove their information. Incomplete/nonpositive information withholds the SE and screening statistic while retaining a computed point. Infit/Outfit retain the legacy variance cutoff (1e-10) and require all contributing rows; FitResponseRows, FitAvailableRows, FitUnavailableRows, FitStatus and FitReason explain withheld complete-cell fit summaries.

  • For two-way mode, use facet_a and facet_b (or interaction_facets with length 2).

  • For higher-order mode, provide interaction_facets with length >= 3.

  • A Person-involving result is a conditional plug-in likelihood screen. It holds fitted JML person measures or MML EAP scores and the other fitted parameters fixed; it is not a jointly fitted Person-by-facet interaction and does not support formal inference or a cell-level fairness decision. The function emits a classed warning when "Person" is requested.

What this screening means

estimate_bias() summarizes additional cell departures from the fitted MFRM. It is best read as a targeted screening tool for potentially noteworthy cells or facet combinations that may merit substantive review.

What this screening does not justify

  • t and Prob. are screening metrics, not formal inferential quantities.

  • A flagged interaction cell is not, by itself, proof of rater bias or construct-irrelevant variance.

  • Non-flagged cells should not be over-read as evidence that interaction effects are absent.

Interpreting output

Use summary for global magnitude, then inspect table for cell-level interaction effects.

Prioritize rows with:

  • larger |Bias Size|, assessed against a substantively chosen threshold in native ability units and its effect on expected scores, rather than a universal small/large-effect rule

  • larger |t| among the screening metrics (the default review rule is \(|t| \ge 2\), not a validated fairness decision)

  • smaller Prob. among the screening metrics

Use Bias Size for the direction of the departure from the baseline model. Expctd Score and Obs-Exp Average use the main-analysis expectations, before adding the cell shift. AfterBiasExpectedScore and AfterBiasObsExpAverage retain the remaining discrepancy after fitting it. Cell t reference df uses weighted count minus 1. This matches the executed FACETS 4.5.0 equal-count binary example; a manual count-minus-2 description is a distinct convention and does not establish version-wide equivalence. DFUnrounded retains count minus one, including nonpositive values. A nonpositive value withholds d.f., DFDisplay and Prob.; a finite point and conditional information SE can remain available. For positive df, DFDisplay rounds to the nearest integer (halves upward) for RSM/PCM display comparison only. d.f. and Prob. use the continuous reference. ProbabilityReference, ProbabilityStatus and ProbabilityReason identify the reference distribution and distinguish available conditional or extreme-adjusted tails from unavailable df, statistics or numerical results. These fields describe Prob., not the separate GPCM likelihood-ratio tail.

Checked FACETS 4.5.0 fractional-count tails are reproduced by extending an integer-df finite-sum formula to fractional df. That extension is not the continuous-df Student distribution and can change a 0.05 screening flag. mfrmr retains the continuous Student tail, independently checked by density integration. This explains the checked output behavior without claiming access to the executable's implementation or general finite-sample validity. The all-zero chi_sq screen sums squared bias/SE ratios without centering; its df is the number of cells. It requires at least two cells and complete cell estimates and SEs. Otherwise its statistic, degrees of freedom and tail area are missing, with available-cell counts and a reason.

summary() reports available and unavailable screening tail-area counts. With none available, screen-positive counts are NA, not zero. Bonferroni/Holm summaries use the full number of retained cells in this interaction, including unavailable cells; they do not include omitted or unobserved cells or other interactions from estimate_all_bias(). Adjustment does not validate the underlying plug-in tail areas or establish formal family-wise error control.

iteration records changes between repeated estimates of the same conditional cell problems. These passes do not refit person or facet parameters, and increasing max_iter does not turn this screen into a jointly fitted interaction model.

Typical workflow

  1. Fit and diagnose model.

  2. Run estimate_bias(...) for target interaction facets.

  3. Review summary(bias) and bias$table.

  4. Visualize/report via plot(x, type = "bias") and build_fixed_reports().

Interpreting key output columns

In bias$table, the most-used columns are:

  • Bias Size: estimated additional cell shift \(b_{jc}\) in native ability units; in GPCM, adjacent log odds change by \(a b_{jc}\)

  • t and Prob.: screening metrics, not formal inferential quantities

  • S.E.: conditional information-based SE of the cell shift, with the calibration held fixed

  • Obs-Exp Average: observed-minus-baseline-expected average on the raw-score metric

  • for GPCM, LR ChiSq, LR Prob., and Profile CI Lower / Profile CI Upper: conditional profile-likelihood checks for a single additive bias shift, holding the fitted person, facet, step, and slope estimates fixed. Calibration uncertainty is not propagated. Check Profile CI Status: limited by search range marks a retained search limit, not a computed likelihood-ratio endpoint. These are screening approximations, not formal fairness tests.

The chi_sq element screens whether all interaction cells equal zero, using diagonal conditional SEs. It is not a full covariance test. Recreate older bias results with current diagnostics and estimate_bias(); saved old expected-score and chi-square definitions are not relabeled.

Recommended next step

Use plot(x, type = "bias") to inspect the flagged cells visually, then integrate the result with DFF, linking, or substantive scoring review before making formal claims about fairness or invariance. Save the mfrm_bias object for repeat use. bias_interaction_report() adds explicit screening rules without refitting; plotting the saved report keeps those rules. mfrm_results() has a separate bias-screen collection route; saving a standalone bias result does not automatically attach it there.

References

  • Linacre, J. M. (1989). Many-Facet Rasch Measurement. MESA Press. (FACETS Table 13 corresponds to the bias / interaction estimation that this helper implements.)

  • Eckes, T. (2005). Examining rater effects in TestDaF writing and speaking performance assessments: A many-facet Rasch analysis. Language Assessment Quarterly, 2(3), 197-221.

  • Eckes, T. (2015). Introduction to many-facet Rasch measurement: Analyzing and evaluating rater-mediated assessments (2nd ed.). Peter Lang.

  • Myford, C. M., & Wolfe, E. W. (2003). Detecting and measuring rater effects using many-facet Rasch measurement: Part I. Journal of Applied Measurement, 4(4), 386-422.

  • Myford, C. M., & Wolfe, E. W. (2004). Detecting and measuring rater effects using many-facet Rasch measurement: Part II. Journal of Applied Measurement, 5(2), 189-227.

Saved-result reuse

The returned fit_identity records the fitted analysis for reuse with reports and exports. Recreate older results from the saved fit and matching diagnostics using the original screening options; no model refit is needed. See mfrmr_compatibility_layer for migration instructions.

See also

interaction_effect_table(), build_fixed_reports(), build_apa_outputs()

Examples

toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_bias")
fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score", method = "JML", maxit = 300)
diag <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none")
bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diag, facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion", max_iter = 2)
s_bias <- summary(bias)
s_bias$overview
#> # A tibble: 1 × 22
#>   FacetPair        InteractionOrder InteractionMode Cells Points ScreenAvailable
#>   <chr>                       <int> <chr>           <int>  <int>           <int>
#> 1 Rater x Criteri…                2 pairwise           16     16              16
#> # ℹ 16 more variables: ScreenUnavailable <int>, MeanAbsBias <dbl>,
#> #   MaxAbsBias <dbl>, ScreenPositive <int>, ScreeningCut <dbl>,
#> #   BonferroniScreenPositive <int>, HolmScreenPositive <int>,
#> #   SupportsFormalInference <lgl>, FormalInferenceEligible <lgl>,
#> #   PrimaryReportingEligible <lgl>, ClassificationSystem <chr>,
#> #   ReportingUse <chr>, Significant <int>, SignificantCut <dbl>,
#> #   BonferroniSignificant <int>, HolmSignificant <int>
# This example uses the default RSM, so Bias Size is also in logit units.
# `Significant` counts cells crossing the screening rule, not proven bias.
# The `BonferroniSignificant` /
#   `HolmSignificant` columns count cells that survive multiple-
#   testing adjustment to screening tail areas. Zero flags do not
#   establish absence of bias or equivalence.
s_bias$top_rows
#> # A tibble: 10 × 19

# An illustrative review rule is |t| > 2 and |Bias Size| > 0.5 logits.
# Choose the effect threshold substantively; these cutoffs do not
#   establish statistical reliability;
#   inspect cell counts, uncertainty and substantive consequences.
p_bias <- plot(bias, type = "bias", draw = FALSE)
p_bias$data$plot
